incidente.resumo: On 17 October 2016 a controller in King's College London's principal HP 3PAR storage system in the Strand Data Centre failed without user impact; after HP replaced it the system went offline and many disks failed, losing all data on the device, which HP later attributed to a firmware flaw. Backups on the same device were lost and tape backups were unreliable or excluded some data, so some data was lost; some data was restored from a retired backup device and other data was recreated from other sources.
servicos_afetados: King's College London core IT systems and data

descricao.texto: One of the four controllers in the principal HP storage system failed with no user impact; after the replacement, the system went offline and many disks started failing. The text does not say how the failure was noticed.
trechos:
On the 17th October 2016 one of the four controllers within the principal HP storage system located in the Strand Data
Centre failed.
There was no user impact.

However, the system went offline and
simultaneously many of the storage disks within it started failing leading to a complete loss of data.

gatilho.texto: On 17 October 2016 one of the four controllers in the principal HP storage system in the Strand Data Centre failed, without user impact, and HP hardware engineers arrived on site to replace the failed component.
trechos:
On the 17th October 2016 one of the four controllers within the principal HP storage system located in the Strand Data
Centre failed.
There was no user impact.

HP hardware engineers then arrived on site to replace the component that
had failed.

descricao.texto: After the replacement the storage system went offline and many of its disks started failing, leading to a complete loss of data. An HP assessment later established that the inability of the storage system to return to service after the defective hardware was replaced was due to a flaw in the firmware responsible for keeping the hardware controllers functional.
trechos:
However, the system went offline and
simultaneously many of the storage disks within it started failing leading to a complete loss of data.

It was later established, in an assessment of the incident by HP, that the inability of the storage system to return to
service after the defective hardware was replaced was due to a flaw in the firmware responsible for keeping the
hardware controllers functional.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: HP had issued an updated firmware version weeks before the incident which, according to HP, would have allowed the replacement controller to be installed without a service outage; it had not been applied before the incident.
trechos:
HP had issued an updated version of the firmware weeks before the incident which
they claim would have allowed the replacement controller to be installed in the storage system without a service outage.
The IT team had not had the opportunity to apply this routine firmware update before the incident.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: Operating system and volume level snapshot backups were kept in a separate partition of the same HP 3PAR machine and were not replicated, so the hardware failure also lost this backup data, leaving the tape backups as the only available backups.
trechos: 2. The operating system level snapshots (1st level) and
volume level snapshots (2nd level) being backed up in a
separate partition within the same HP 3PAR machine.
The back up data (above) was not replicated.

The hardware failure caused the Strand HP 3PAR storage device to lose
  all data that was stored in the machine. This meant that only available
back ups were the tape drives.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: Tape backups failed regularly and some folders were not backed up properly for several months, while Daily Service Review updates reported backups as a success when they contained repeated failures; the review states the importance of the tape backups was not understood and backup procedures were not followed completely.
trechos: Tape backups failed regularly and some folders were not backed up properly for
Daily Service Review (DSR) updates on the tape back up status
were not being reported correctly (e.g. backups were declared as a success when
they contained repeated failures to back up some shared drives).

The cause of the backup failure was due to the IT technical team not fully understanding the importance of the tape
back ups within the overall backup system and not following the back up procedures completely.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: Some data had consciously never been backed up on tape due to capacity constraints, and the potential impact was never communicated to the College; as the Netbackup solution did not work correctly, shared drive data was lost and had to be recreated from other sources.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: The performance of the backup systems had never been tested, making accurate recovery time estimates difficult; full Disaster Recovery tests had not been carried out, and the review states they would have shown the backup systems were not functioning correctly.
trechos:
The response team produced regular progress updates to the
affected user communities, though it was difficult to provide accurate recovery time estimates on account of the fact that
the performance of backup systems had never been tested.
IT has not been able to convince users on the need for doing full
Disaster Recovery tests and negotiate windows for these to occur.
Had these occurred it would have demonstrated that the
backup systems were not functioning correctly..

fatores_contribuintes.texto: There was no catalogue or user-to-folder mapping of what data users stored in shared drives, which hampered the recovery effort.
trechos: The IT team did not know what
type of data was being stored by the users in shared drives. Nor did
the IT team have a catalogue or user to folder mapping. All of which
hampered the recovery effort

observacoes: External review by PA Consulting for the College; recommendations are addressed to the College. The PDF extraction scrambles columns and the incident timeline appendix, so timeline dates were not used; the appendix says the BCP Silver team handed over recovery work in the week ending Friday 25th Nov, but no end of impact is stated, so duracao is null. Office 365 and the KEATS system were not impacted. The report also lists organizational findings (IT governance, user engagement, team growth) and recommendations not included here. The cause of the disk failures themselves is not explained beyond HP's firmware assessment.
